newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Observer
BOURSE REGULATOR OKAYS SHORT SALE WITH CONDITIONS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) gave its clearance to short selling. The market watchdog, however, decided to regularise it by imposition of certain curbs, including the seller having to declare his short position at the close of trading each day. The stock exchanges would also be asked to appropriate margin on the short sale. SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta said a committee of experts would be set up shortly to work out modalities for implementing these decisions.
INDIA TO INCREASE ACCESS TO TELECORN SECTOR

India will present an improved offer on providing access to its telecom market in the forthcoming Singapore Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organisation. The meet, to be held in December, is scheduled to discuss the progress of the multilateral talks on liberalising the global trade in telecom services. The Indian offer includes the commitment to allow foreign equity up to 49 percent in basic telecom services and opening up of long-distant and international telecom markets in a phased manner before 2004.
The Times Of India
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY DEMANDS GOVERNOR'S RECALL

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) plans to mount an attack on the United Front (UF) government by urging the President to immediately recall the Uttar Pradesh (UP) governor. An 11-member BJP delegation led by former premier A.B. Vajpayee met the president to seek his intervention to end the constitutional impasse in UP following the Assembly polls. According to the BJP, the governor had played a controversial role by not inviting the BJP to form the government in UP even though it was the single largest party in the state. Absolute majority was not mandatory for forming a government, the BJP said, which had fallen short of the required majority in the last assembly polls.
The Hindustan Times
FORMER PREMIER BOWS DOWN TO PARTY LEADERSHIP

The supporters of Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader P.V. Narasimha Rao agreed that the CPP would be subservient to party president Sitaram Kesri and the Congress Working Committee's resolutions. The sudden tactical retreat by Rao's aides came as a major gain for Kesri's efforts to consolidate his control over Congress. The change in the attitude was linked to the announcement of polls for 19 positions in the CPP executive committee by December 10. Party sources said the contests would be an acid test between the supporters of Rao and Kesri.
The Pioneer
BJP-BSP REACH PACT FOR UPPER HOUSE POLLS

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will have an agreement with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) for contesting the November 29 by-election to three Rajya Sabha (Upper House) seats in Uttar Pradesh. Senior BJP leader Kalyan Singh said the BJP would field its candidates on two seats while the BSP would contest one seat from the state. He, however, clarified the adjustment with the BSP was confined to Rajya Sabha elections alone.
The Economic Times
PETRO PRICE HIKE PROPOSAL TO FACE ANGRY OPPOSITION

Prime Minister Deve Gowda's efforts at getting the nod of political parties to hike the price of diesel has run into trouble. Both the partners of the ruling cloaition and the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party have decided to oppose the move at the meeting of parliament's consultative committee. For the prime minister, who had aimed to use the meeting as a means to reach a consensus among the parties on the issue, the development has come as a rude shock. Gowda had promised to go in for the hike only after ensuring a consensus on the matter. The government will now have to take some unpopular steps for tackling the oil pool deficit, which may touch 150 billion rupees at the end of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
FINANCE MINISTER EAGER TO STEP UP CREDIT TO INDUSTRY

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will meet the chiefs of the public sector commercial bank on November 29 to explore measures to step up credit to the industry. The Finance Ministry is learnt to have been concerned about the dip in credit disbursement between March-September 1996. According to banking circles, there could be a real recession if the negative growth in credit experienced during April-September 1996 continued. The Finance Minister's move is aimed at dispelling such fears about an imminent slow down in the economy.
ISRO TO PARTNER MICROSOFT, MCCAW CELLULAR

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to be a major partner in the Microsoft and McCaw Cellular Communication promoted $9 billion 'Internet in the sky' project. Talks with ISRO to build and launch a number of the proposed 840 low earth orbit spacecraft began in April, 1996. ISRO sources said preliminary discussions were on and announcement of the decision could coincide with Bill Gates' visit to India in February, 1997. The project, called Teledesic, would use a constellation of satellites to offer Internet services to all parts of the world. Sources said ISRO was being considered as it had demonstrated its capability in building satellites and launching the at competitive costs.
LCC, TELECOM DENMARK PULL OUT OF BPL VENTURES

Two foreign collaborators, LCC Investments and Telecom Denmark, have pulled out of the BPL group's telecommunication ventures. Britain's LCC Investments sold its holding in BPL Mobile Communications, the cellular phone service operator in Bombay, while Telecom Denmark refused to subscribe to its equity in BPL Wireless Telecommunications, which offers paging services in some states in southern India. LCC, which had a 12 percent stake in BPL Mobile, wanted to sell its stake since early this year, after BPL insisted it invest in the company at a premium. On the other hand, Telecom Denmark took a strategic decision to pull out of all its joint ventures in India.
INDIAN OIL CORP GETS TWO WESTERN OFFSHORE BLOCKS

The Oil Ministry decided to award D-1 and D-18 oilfield blocks in the Western Offshore region to Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) on a nomination basis. The move came despite the ministry's decision to put on hold a plan to offer small-sized discovered oilfields in a new bidding round. The decision would enable IOC, the giant refining and marketing company, to diversify into exploration. The ministry, however, decided that it would not award the other public sector downstream major having, ambitious upstream blocks, on a nomination basis.
Financial Express
ICICI TO RAISE TWO BLN RUPEES VIA BOND AUCTION

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) has decided to adopt an auction system for raising two billion rupees via an issue of bonds for a maturity period of 15 months. Sources said ICICI would raise resources through a Dutch system of auction in an attempt to price the security via the open market for raising resources. ICICI's bonds would have a threshold investment-limit of one million rupees and would be basically targeted at institutional investors, sources added.
NPC, ATOMERG TO BUILD NUCLEAR REACTORS JOINTLY

The Nuclear Power Corporation (NPC) has identified Atomerg of Russia as its partner for building two nuclear reactors. These power plants (four units each) will have a combined capacity of 2000 megawatts, equal to the total capacity of NPC's six operating units now. The tie-up will entail know-how transfer and credit for equipment supply from Russia. The mode of acquiring equipment from third countries will be finalised soon. The nuclear power units will be built at Kudunkulum in Tamil Nadu.
HINDUSTAN CIBA-GEIGY TURNOVER UP

Hindustan Ciba-Geigy (HCG) reported a 20.83 percent increase in turnover to 3.04 billion rupees and a 10 percent rise in net profit to 176.2 million rupees for the half-year ended September 1996. Turnover and net profit in the same period of the previous year stood at 2.51 billion rupees and 160.2 million rupees respectively. HCG's exports increased 120 percent to 435 million rupees from the previous period's 198 million rupees. Growth in exports came from the dyestuffs, crop protection and pharmaceutical businesses. The HCG board approved schemes for demerger of the speciality chemicals undertaking and merger of Sandoz India with the company.
FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES INCREASE TO $18.429 BILLION

Foreign exchange reserves increased by $1.385 billion from the end of fiscal 1995/96 (April-March) and stood at $18.429 billion by September end, 1996. The Finance Ministry's monthly economic report for October 1996 said foreign exchange reserves (excluding gold and Special Drawing Rights) stood at $17.044 billion at the end of 1995/96. Exports in dollars terms during April-August, 1996, went up by 9.8 percent as compared to a rise of 28 percent during April-August, 1995. Imports soared by 4.7 percent as against 37.1 percent during April-August, 1995. Inflation rate was 6.4 percent as one week ending October 5. 1996. The rupee appreciated against Deutsche Mark, Franc and Yen and depreciated against the US dollar and Pound Sterling in September 1996.
DCM DAEWOO'S NET RISES 61 PCT

Buoyed by a 40 percent market share in the mid-sized car segment, DCM-Daewoo Motors Ltd reported a net profit of 280 million rupees for the first six months of the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) on an increased sales turnover of 5.84 billion rupees. The net profit was up 61 percent from 175 million rupees reported in the corresponding period last year. Gross sales registered a 327 percent growth, with the turnover climbing up substantially from 1.14 billion rupees in the first six months of 1995/96.
Business Standard
BOMBAY BOURSE TO SET UP TRADE GUARANTEE FUND

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) approved setting up of trade guarantee fund with a corpus of 1.72 billion rupees. Sources said the fund would guarantee all trades transacted on the exchange, by providing the money value of shares to the aggrieved broker in case the opposing broker defaulted. The entire process of setting up a trade guarantee fund would be in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India's requirements for BSE's on-line trading expansion, sources said.
ADB KEEN TO FUND LNDO-BANGLA POWER LINK

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is keen to fund the proposed $15 million power transmission link between West Bengal and Bangladesh. The proposed link would be the first of a series of transmission links between the two countries for regular exchange of power. The 100-km link is expected to cost around 500 million rupees. However, there would be additional expenditure for transformers at both ends. The power link may also be utilised for an additional telecommunication link between the two countries. The two countries are contemplating three links from West Bengal and Meghalaya to various points in Bangladesh for exchange of power.
AUDITORS SOUND ALARM BELL ON BPL CELLULAR

KPMG Peat Marwick is afraid that BPL Cellular Holdings may not survive as a company. The observations came close on the heels of an accumulated 4.36 billion rupee loss declared by the company in the prospectus for its current $185-million American Depository Receipt issue. Peat Marwick, the company's auditor, said BPL Holdings' working capital deficiency and operating losses incurred during the build-up phase of its mobile and radio paging network, net capital deficiency and significant capital needs for setting up these networks had raised doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern. The company made an operating loss of 485 million rupees in fiscal 1996.
